page: Microsoft Azure M128-32ms is a memory-intensive server instance belonging to the MS family, virtualized on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280L processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 3892.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 121.62 GB per core. Additionally, it includes 4194 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 10% tier. However, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores reach average levels. Memory bandwidth write operations for large blocks are strong, placing in the top 25%, while read-only memory bandwidth remains average.

Given the massive memory allocation relative to the vCPU count, this server offers high memory density, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads rather than compute-heavy tasks. The server is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers such as Redis, and enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM and local storage without demanding high single-thread CPU performance.
